outcome: Live births (via cesarean section, spontaneous vaginal delivery)
Subsequent pathology diagnoses (epithelioid trophoblastic tumors, persistent APSN, PSN, no abnormalities)
Histopathologic characteristics (cytologic atypia, Ki-67 proliferation index, immunohistochemical profiles)
cohort: The study included 35 women diagnosed with atypical placental site nodules (APSN) from the New England Trophoblastic Disease Center registry between 2005 and 2022, with 29 having available clinical and demographic data.
finding: APSN is a rare form of gestational trophoblastic proliferation with uncertain malignant potential and a high persistence rate, where normal obstetric outcomes are possible but definitive management often remains hysterectomy.
mod_finding: Subsequent obstetrical outcomes mentioned included 2 cesarean sections and 1 spontaneous vaginal delivery.
